parameters.name: ad_user
parameters.description: Active Directory username. Use when authenticating with an Active Directory user rather than service principal.

parameters.name: adfs_authority_url
parameters.description: Azure AD authority url. Use when authenticating with Username/password, and has your own ADFS authority.

parameters.name: api_profile
parameters.description: Selects an API profile to use when communicating with Azure services. Default value of latest is appropriate for public clouds; future values will allow use with Azure Stack. Default: "latest"

parameters.name: append_tags
parameters.description: Use to control if tags field is canonical or just appends to existing tags. When canonical, any tags not found in the tags parameter will be removed from the object’s metadata. Choices: false true ← (default)

parameters.name: auth_source
parameters.description: Controls the source of the credentials to use for authentication. Can also be set via the ANSIBLE_AZURE_AUTH_SOURCE environment variable. When set to auto (the default) the precedence is module parameters -> env -> credential_file -> cli. When set to env, the credentials will be read from the environment variables When set to credential_file, it will read the profile from ~/.azure/credentials. When set to cli, the credentials will be sources from the Azure CLI profile. subscription_id or the environment variable AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID can be used to identify the subscription ID if more than one is present otherwise the default az cli subscription is used. When set to msi, the host machine must be an azure resource with an enabled MSI extension. subscription_id or the environment variable AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID can be used to identify the subscription ID if the resource is granted access to more than one subscription, otherwise the first subscription is chosen. The msi was added in Ansible 2.6. Choices: "auto" ← (default) "cli" "credential_file" "env" "msi"

parameters.name: cert_validation_mode
parameters.description: Controls the certificate validation behavior for Azure endpoints. By default, all modules will validate the server certificate, but when an HTTPS proxy is in use, or against Azure Stack, it may be necessary to disable this behavior by passing ignore. Can also be set via credential file profile or the AZURE_CERT_VALIDATION environment variable. Choices: "ignore" "validate"

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: Azure client ID. Use when authenticating with a Service Principal or Managed Identity (msi). Can also be set via the AZURE_CLIENT_ID environment variable.

parameters.name: cloud_environment
parameters.description: For cloud environments other than the US public cloud, the environment name (as defined by Azure Python SDK, eg, AzureChinaCloud, AzureUSGovernment), or a metadata discovery endpoint URL (required for Azure Stack). Can also be set via credential file profile or the AZURE_CLOUD_ENVIRONMENT environment variable. Default: "AzureCloud"

parameters.name: disable_instance_discovery
parameters.description: Determines whether or not instance discovery is performed when attempting to authenticate. Setting this to true will completely disable both instance discovery and authority validation. This functionality is intended for use in scenarios where the metadata endpoint cannot be reached such as in private clouds or Azure Stack. The process of instance discovery entails retrieving authority metadata from https://login.microsoft.com/ to validate the authority. By setting this to **True**, the validation of the authority is disabled. As a result, it is crucial to ensure that the configured authority host is valid and trustworthy. Set via credential file profile or the AZURE_DISABLE_INSTANCE_DISCOVERY environment variable. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: enabled
parameters.description: Specifies whether automatic scaling is enabled for the resource. Choices: false true ← (default)

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: location of the resource.

parameters.name: log_mode
parameters.description: Parent argument.

parameters.name: log_path
parameters.description: Parent argument.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: name of the resource.

parameters.name: notifications
parameters.description: The collection of notifications.

parameters.name: custom_emails
parameters.description: The custom e-mails list. This value can be null or empty, in which case this attribute will be ignored.

parameters.name: send_to_subscription_administrator
parameters.description: A value indicating whether to send email to subscription administrator. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: send_to_subscription_co_administrators
parameters.description: A value indicating whether to send email to subscription co-administrators. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: webhooks
parameters.description: The list of webhook notifications service uri.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Active Directory user password. Use when authenticating with an Active Directory user rather than service principal.

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: Security profile found in ~/.azure/credentials file.

parameters.name: profiles
parameters.description: The collection of automatic scaling profiles that specify different scaling parameters for different time periods. A maximum of 20 profiles can be specified.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: The number of instances that will be set if metrics are not available for evaluation. The default is only used if the current instance count is lower than the default.

parameters.name: fixed_date_end
parameters.description: The specific date-time end for the profile. This element is not used if the Recurrence element is used.

parameters.name: fixed_date_start
parameters.description: The specific date-time start for the profile. This element is not used if the Recurrence element is used.

parameters.name: fixed_date_timezone
parameters.description: The specific date-time timezone for the profile. This element is not used if the Recurrence element is used.

parameters.name: max_count
parameters.description: The maximum number of instances for the resource. The actual maximum number of instances is limited by the cores that are available in the subscription.

parameters.name: min_count
parameters.description: The minimum number of instances for the resource.

parameters.name: recurrence_days
parameters.description: The days of repeating times at which this profile begins. This element is not used if the FixedDate element is used.

parameters.name: recurrence_frequency
parameters.description: How often the schedule profile should take effect. If this value is Week, meaning each week will have the same set of profiles. This element is not used if the FixedDate element is used. Choices: "None" ← (default) "Second" "Minute" "Hour" "Day" "Week" "Month" "Year"

parameters.name: recurrence_hours
parameters.description: The hours of repeating times at which this profile begins. This element is not used if the FixedDate element is used.

parameters.name: recurrence_mins
parameters.description: The mins of repeating times at which this profile begins. This element is not used if the FixedDate element is used.

parameters.name: recurrence_timezone
parameters.description: The timezone of repeating times at which this profile begins. This element is not used if the FixedDate element is used.

parameters.name: rules
parameters.description: The collection of rules that provide the triggers and parameters for the scaling action. A maximum of 10 rules can be specified.

parameters.name: cooldown
parameters.description: The amount of time (minutes) to wait since the last scaling action before this action occurs. It must be between 1 ~ 10080.

parameters.name: dimensions
parameters.description: List of dimension conditions.

parameters.name: dimension_name
parameters.description: Name of the dimension.

parameters.name: operator
parameters.description: The dimension operator. Only Equals and NotEquals are supported. Choices: "Equals" "NotEquals"

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: List of dimension values.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: Whether the scaling action increases or decreases the number of instances. Choices: "Increase" "Decrease"

parameters.name: divide_per_instance
parameters.description: A value indicating whether metric should divide per instance. Choices: false true

parameters.name: metric_name
parameters.description: The name of the metric that defines what the rule monitors.

parameters.name: metric_namespace
parameters.description: The namespace of the metric that defines what the rule monitors.

parameters.name: metric_resource_uri
parameters.description: The resource identifier of the resource the rule monitors.

parameters.name: statistic
parameters.description: How the metrics from multiple instances are combined. Choices: "Average" ← (default) "Min" "Max" "Sum"

parameters.name: threshold
parameters.description: The threshold of the metric that triggers the scale action. Default: 70.0

parameters.name: time_aggregation
parameters.description: How the data that is collected should be combined over time. Choices: "Average" ← (default) "Minimum" "Maximum" "Total" "Count"

parameters.name: time_grain
parameters.description: The granularity(minutes) of metrics the rule monitors. Must be one of the predefined values returned from metric definitions for the metric. Must be between 1 ~ 720.

parameters.name: time_window
parameters.description: The range of time(minutes) in which instance data is collected. This value must be greater than the delay in metric collection, which can vary from resource-to-resource. Must be between 5 ~ 720.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The type of action that should occur when the scale rule fires. Choices: "PercentChangeCount" "ExactCount" "ChangeCount"

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The number of instances that are involved in the scaling action. This value must be 1 or greater.

parameters.name: resource_group
parameters.description: Resource group of the resource.

parameters.name: secret
parameters.description: Azure client secret. Use when authenticating with a Service Principal.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Assert the state of the virtual network. Use present to create or update and absent to delete. Choices: "present" ← (default) "absent"

parameters.name: subscription_id
parameters.description: Your Azure subscription Id.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: Dictionary of string:string pairs to assign as metadata to the object. Metadata tags on the object will be updated with any provided values. To remove tags set append_tags option to false. Currently, Azure DNS zones and Traffic Manager services also don’t allow the use of spaces in the tag. Azure Front Door doesn’t support the use of Azure Automation and Azure CDN only support 15 tags on resources.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: The identifier of the resource to apply autoscale setting. It could be the resource id string. It also could be a dict contains the name, subscription_id, namespace, types, resource_group of the resource.

parameters.name: tenant
parameters.description: Azure tenant ID. Use when authenticating with a Service Principal.

parameters.name: thumbprint
parameters.description: The thumbprint of the private key specified in x509_certificate_path. Use when authenticating with a Service Principal. Required if x509_certificate_path is defined.

parameters.name: x509_certificate_path
parameters.description: Path to the X509 certificate used to create the service principal in PEM format. The certificate must be appended to the private key. Use when authenticating with a Service Principal.

examples:
- name: Create an auto scale
  azure_rm_autoscale:
    target: "/subscriptions/xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx/resourceGroups/myResourceGroup/providers/Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachineScaleSets/myVmss"
    enabled: true
    profiles:
      - count: '1'
        recurrence_days:
          - Monday
        name: Auto created scale condition
        recurrence_timezone: China Standard Time
        recurrence_mins:
          - '0'
        min_count: '1'
        max_count: '1'
        recurrence_frequency: Week
        recurrence_hours:
          - '18'
    name: scale
    resource_group: myResourceGroup

- name: Create an auto scale with complicated profile
  azure_rm_autoscale:
    target: "/subscriptions/xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx/resourceGroups/myResourceGroup/providers/Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachineScaleSets
               /myVmss"
    enabled: true
    profiles:
      - count: '1'
        recurrence_days:
          - Monday
        name: Auto created scale condition 0
        rules:
          - time_aggregation: Average
            time_window: 10
            direction: Increase
            metric_name: Percentage CPU
            metric_resource_uri: "/subscriptions/xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx/resourceGroups/myResourceGroup/providers/Microsoft.Compute/virtua
                                lMachineScaleSets/vmss"
            value: '1'
            threshold: 70
            cooldown: 5
            time_grain: 1
            statistic: Average
            operator: GreaterThan
            type: ChangeCount
            dimensions:
              - dimension_name: AppName
                operator: Equals
                values:
                  - App1
                  - App2
        max_count: '1'
        recurrence_mins:
          - '0'
        min_count: '1'
        recurrence_timezone: China Standard Time
        recurrence_frequency: Week
        recurrence_hours:
          - '6'
    notifications:
      - email_admin: true
        email_co_admin: false
        custom_emails:
          - yuwzho@microsoft.com
    name: scale
    resource_group: myResourceGroup

- name: Delete an Azure Auto Scale Setting
  azure_rm_autoscale:
    state: absent
    resource_group: myResourceGroup
    name: scale
